Fellow Voaters, have you thought about running away and starting a fresh new life? Or if you have done this, was it worth it?

Used to be a jazz musician. Was short on money really bad one month, so went to work in coal mines and oil refineries. I realized how much I enjoyed hard work and natural resources. I'm now an oil and gas lawyer. My old jazz musician friends are confused. My lawyer friends think it's weird.
Was it something that opened your eyes on the reality or just pure need for money that drove you to find your real self?

Good question. Originally, I was enamored with the idea of being a starving musician. Something about that element proving I was passionately doing what I wanted because I believe in it. I liked that.

But soon, all my friends with engineering degrees, business degrees, accounting degrees,etc., they all had real jobs and money. They were taking girls on really nice dates, and there I was bragging about eating ramen and practicing my horn 6 hours per day while practically begging for gigs.

When I couldn't make rent, and was forced to make tough decisions, luckily my dad hooked me up with a great paying job in a coal mine. I was finally able to buy some new clothes. Take girls on nice dates. Pay rent. Pitch in a little for beer runs.

I realized that hard work is a means to ends. And there was something oddly satisfying about society finally rewarding me for my hard work. The reward was money. And I was in control of that money. I was in control of very few aspects of my life before that.

That is a very interesting story, thanks for sharing. I would not have imagined like that. It is true that hard work feels satisfying, especially the work that you can observe results of in one or the other form.
How positive this community is. Thanks for asking, it was a nice way to be introspective.

Yup.

I was young, and had dropped out of college. I was engaged to this woman who I had loved since I met her. She left me for another man, and I was heartbroken. I crawled inside the bottle for a week, then decided I would just pack my bags and leave. Left the apartment with twenty dollars in my pocket, and just started walking. Spent the next six or seven years on the road. Did a little of everything. Lumper at a truck stop. Carney. Dishwasher at any place that needed someone. Lumberjack. Repo man. Fortune teller. Roofer. Juggler. Hundreds of jobs, countless cities. All trying to get her out of my head.

Must have worked. Didn't see her for another twenty years.

It made for some interesting times.

I was/still am Mormon. Was raised very strictly and with very high standards. I turned 19 and was rebelling a bit. My parents (dad and step mom) were straight up annoying as fuck. I tried to be my own man and get my own place, only to be torn down by them at every turn. So I decided enough is enough. I had my own car and that angst of a teen. I packed up my entire room (well everything I could pack up) into my little Mazda 3 hatchback at 1:00am one day. I literally threw everything I owned out of my bedroom window so I wouldn't have to go through the house. I got in my car and drove straight through to Utah from Texas. A 17 hour drive in one sitting. I had friends up there and went to live with them. I lived up there for 6 months and decided to come back for my now wife. I told my parents that I'm going to do my own thing from then on and I still loved them but I was an adult. Jokes on me, in 23 now and still figuring shit out.

Yes, it is worth it. I'd suggest it to just about anyone who has second thoughts about their life's path where they are at. I left where I was from with $21 and a backpack full of clothes. The $21 ran out by St Louis. We had to work gas stations to get gas money to get the rest of the way west. I got my backpack full of clothes stolen my first week out west and lived with nothing but the clothes on my back for the first 6 weeks while living on the street and camping outside. But I found my way and built a life out west. Twenty four years later I still live out here and have only gone back three times and those were for funerals. I don't regret a thing.
I've got a Spanish speaking best friend and we both live in Texas, so I'm thinking if we ever got into some kind of bad trouble, we could actually cut and run to Mexico.
